name: Read my bill (Test drive)
idea: Reads my electricity bill, keeps the exact numbers printed on it, and checks that the amount adds up.

cards.title: Read my bill
cards.statement: Reads my electricity bill, keeps the exact numbers printed on it, and checks that the amount adds up.

cards.title: Exactly as printed
cards.statement: Six things are read off the bill and kept exactly as printed: the consumer number, the category, the billing period, the units consumed, the amount payable and the due date. Anything not on the bill is left empty and named, never guessed. Amounts are kept in paise and shown in rupees.

cards.title: Keep every bill
cards.statement: Every bill read is kept as a new row in a bills table, with the file it was read from; nothing is overwritten. The first time with an empty table, the sample bill (a one-page September 2026 bill for 412 units and Rs 3,003.00) is read and kept. Without a database, the sample bill is read straight from its file.

cards.title: The tariff
cards.statement: The amount is checked against a sample domestic tariff kept in a file and named on the screen as a sample: up to 100 units at Rs 5.50, the next 200 at Rs 6.80, the rest at Rs 7.50; a fixed charge of Rs 110 a month; electricity duty of 5 percent on the energy and fixed charges.

cards.title: Building: Read the bill
cards.statement: Building “Read the bill”: its screen is the first page, My bill, for the customer. It shows the six things; Units consumed and Amount payable are figures traced to the bill.

cards.title: Building: Check the amount
cards.statement: Building “Check the amount”: its screen is /check, Does it add up?, for the customer. It says in words whether the bill adds up, then shows the energy charge, the fixed charge, the duty, what it should come to, what the bill asks for and the difference, each a traced figure.

cards.title: What it will not do
cards.statement: It does not pay the bill, read a scanned bill (a picture), or fetch a real supplier's tariff from the web.
